kept.excerpt: The 2026 Tour de France isn’t even halfway over, but Tadej Pogačar carries a 2:42 lead into the first rest day. UAE sport manager Joxean Fernández Matxín told Velo the team had circled stage 6 as the place to land a knockout punch. There are still nearly two weeks left to race, and Matxín cautioned that UAE is taking nothing for granted.
kept.relevance: Rest-day reporting establishes Pogačar’s current advantage and explains UAE’s successful tactics while acknowledging the remaining racing.

kept.excerpt: Tadej Pogačar and UAE Team Emirates-XRG have become the latest squad to be struck by failed air-conditioning at the Tour de France during the first rest day. According to Spanish journalist Sergi López-Egea, the hotel where the Emirati team are staying in the Massif Central is experiencing power issues, with the supply cutting out when guests attempt to switch on the air conditioning units.
kept.relevance: The report identifies a contemporaneous recovery concern during extreme heat that could affect Pogačar and his supporting team.

kept.excerpt: Tadej Pogačar, who has a 2:42 lead over second-place Jonas Vingegaard, stayed safe in yellow. The relentless heat forced organizers to cut 30 km from the route through the department of Corrèze between Malemort and Ussel.
kept.relevance: The latest completed-stage report independently confirms Pogačar’s lead entering the rest day and documents the heat affecting race operations.

kept.excerpt: UAE Team Emirates set the pace for the peloton during part of Stage 9, where Tadej Pogacar retained the Yellow Jersey. “It was a very hard day. I hope tomorrow will be a calm day, with a nice easy spin and some good rest.”
kept.publisher: Tour de France / A.S.O. — official rider interview
kept.relevance: The organizer’s dated interview confirms Pogačar remained in the race and retained the overall lead after stage 9, with fatigue and recovery on his agenda.

kept.excerpt: The four-time winner of the race attacked on the slopes of the Col du Tourmalet to claim a 23rd stage win, his eleventh in the Pyrenees, his second in this edition. Pogacar kept pushing, covering the final 43 kilometres alone to open massive gaps at Gavarnie-Gèdre. Jonas Vingegaard finished second (+2’38’’), ahead of a small group led by Isaac del Toro (+2’57’’).
kept.publisher: Tour de France / A.S.O. — official stage 6 report
kept.relevance: The official race report records the mountain performance that created Pogačar’s substantial advantage over his principal rival.

kept.excerpt: The challenge set for the field of the Tour de France between 4 and 26 July was unveiled before an audience of almost 3,500 at the Palais des Congrès de Paris. Following the Grand Départ in Barcelona, the race will pay a visit to each of the five mountain ranges in France. The only individual time trial will take place against the backdrop of Lake Geneva (stage 16). The double finish on the Alpe d’Huez comprises stages 19 and 20.
kept.publisher: Tour de France / A.S.O. — official route announcement, “In Crescendo”
kept.relevance: The dated organizer announcement verifies the scheduled race window and the major time-trial and mountain challenges still ahead at the cutoff.

kept.excerpt: As the Slovenian superstar claimed his fourth overall victory at the Tour, he also improved his own record of being the first rider to always place on the podium in his first eight Grand Tours. In the end, the German newcomer stayed in control and on the overall podium: Tadej Pogačar, Jonas Vingegaard (+04’24’’), Florian Lipowitz (+11’09’’).
kept.publisher: Union Cycliste Internationale (UCI) — “Tour de France: Pogačar’s absolute triumph”
kept.relevance: The governing body’s account supplies historical evidence of Pogačar’s Grand Tour consistency and his previous Tour winning margin over Vingegaard.
